instructions: Cut the lamb into 1 1/2 inch pieces and pat them dry. Sprinkle with 1 tsp of the salt and the black pepper. Dice the onion and mince the garlic.

Heat a large heavy pot over medium-high. Add the olive oil. Add half the lamb in a single layer and leave it alone for 4 minutes, until the underside is browned. Turn the pieces and cook for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pot and cook for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens. Return the lamb and any juices to the pot. Add 2 1/2 cups water and scrape up the browned bits.
Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the carrots and potatoes and cut them into 3/4 inch pieces. Chop 1/4 cup of the dill.
Add the carrots and potatoes to the pot. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the lamb and vegetables are tender.

While that cooks, put the rice in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and the last 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Add the peas to the stew and cook for 5 minutes, uncovered, until they're hot and the sauce has thickened a little.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Stir in the dill. Serve over the rice.
method_notes: The honest time is about 2 hours, a long one for a weeknight, so it is better on a day with time at home. No version with 20 or more ratings turned up, so this is a fallback. Cup of Yum (5 from 2 reviews, read from the visible rating) leads: brown the lamb, soften the onion, bloom the tomato paste, then simmer everything with carrot and potato for about 1 hour 15. Almost Turkish Recipes (no rating shown) makes it with beef and grated tomato and finishes with dill. Pomona adds the carrots and potatoes after the lamb has had a head start, and adds the peas at the end so they stay green.
